issues.detail: The Hebrew 'יִרְקַח' means 'to mix/compound (perfume/ointment)', not 'to shave hair'. The Chinese '剃髮' (shave hair) is a mistranslation. Also 'כָּמֹהוּ' means 'like it' (like the anointing oil), and 'יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ עַל זָר' means 'puts any of it on a stranger/outsider', not 'gives him the shaved things'. The Chinese rendering changes the action from compounding the oil and applying it to a stranger to shaving hair and giving the shavings.
